Science Elective with Lab: science course selected from the following: PHYSICS 202/212, CHEM 105, 106, BIOLOGY 106, or 107.

CS Option Course
CS Option Courses: 15 credits of option area courses are required for completion of the degree program. The option courses must be chosen from 300-400-level CS courses and may also include up to 6 credits from the following list: MATH 315, 320, 325, 364, 420, 448, 453, 466, ECE 324, 366, 424, and DATA 319. Other computer science-related courses may be substituted, as approved by the department.

ENGLISH 402 [WRTG]

STAT 360

CS 351

CS Option Courses
CS Option Courses: 15 credits of option area courses are required for completion of the degree program. The option courses must be chosen from 300-400-level CS courses and may also include up to 6 credits from the following list: MATH 315, 320, 325, 364, 420, 448, 453, 466, ECE 324, 366, 424, and DATA 319. Other computer science-related courses may be substituted, as approved by the department.

CS 402 [M]

CS 421

CS Security Option Course
CS Security Option Courses: 3 credits of security option area courses are required for completion of the degree program. These credits are in addition to the 15 credits of CS Option Courses required above. CS Security Option Courses must be chosen from the following courses: CS 425, 426, and 427.

CS Systems Option Course
CS Systems Option Courses: 3 credits of systems option area courses are required for completion of the degree program. These credits are in addition to the 15 credits of CS Option Courses required above. CS Systems Option Courses must be chosen from the following courses: CS 455, 460, and 466.

Complete CS Exit Survey

For the major in the Computer Science degree program on the Vancouver campus, students are admitted to the major upon demonstrating they are ready to take MATH 171 (Calculus I) or higher and making their intentions known to the department. The prerequisites for MATH 171 include MATH 106 with a C or better and MATH 108 with a C or better, or a minimum ALEKS math placement score of 83%.

To keep their status as Computer Science majors and to remain in good academic standing, students must pass CS 121, 122, 166, MATH 171, 172, and PHYSICS 201/211 (or their transfer equivalents) with a grade of C or better and maintain a cumulative GPA of 2.0 or higher.

No courses listed in this schedule of studies may be taken on a pass/fail basis. All listed computer science courses, and their prerequisites, must be completed with a grade of C or better.
